_README: This file is the project's verification ledger. Claims record what is believed true about this project AND the command that proves it. Do not delete or reword claims to make them pass, and never hand-edit a status to 'passing' -- only `ledger run` may do that. If a claim is obsolete, mark it retired with `ledger retire`, which preserves it.

claims.claim: the restore stage measures the source rather than assuming it: blockiness drives strength (fitted to the measured optima - clean 1.06 to 0, crf45 2.23 to 0.66, JPEG q0.12 2.82 to 0.82), and the transform grid's PHASE and PERIOD are detected per axis rather than assumed. Both detections pay off: on a picture shifted 3px, filtering the detected phase leaves blockiness 1.447 where assuming the origin leaves 1.978; on a 4x4 transform grid, filtering as period 4 leaves 1.038 where period 8 leaves 1.202

claims.claim: the neural upscaler's cost is arithmetic, not an API artifact, so porting the engine to WebGPU would not buy a bigger model: a compute implementation with shader-f16 and workgroup shared-memory tiling, verified against the same PyTorch reference as the GLSL port (interior max 0.31/255), runs the shipped 8-filter model at 4.25 ms vs the fragment path's 4.71 (1.11x) and a 16-filter model at 11.11 ms vs 14.62 (1.32x) - against only 8.85 ms of headroom once the classical chain has spent 7.85 of the 16.7 ms budget. It still does not fit, and even if it did the measured payoff was +0.19 dB

claims.claim: the neural upscaler's shipped architecture is not what limits it: a controlled four-variant experiment (same data, same seed, same 60 epochs) scored baseline 8 filters x 4 layers at 31.111 dB validation, ArtCNN's long skip connection at 31.017, six layers at 31.072, and six layers plus skip at 30.332. The baseline wins; neither the skip nor the extra depth helps. Depth was worth testing because cost here is linear in depth and quadratic in width, which is what made the earlier 16-filter attempt unaffordable

claims.claim: denoise is auto-tuned from the source's measured blockiness rather than fixed, and the curve was fitted on a metric that cannot be fooled by blurring: across a ladder of JPEG degradations plus the real rip it lands on the detail-safe optimum within 0.02 (clean 1.06 -> 0, q0.6 1.46 -> 0.6, q0.35 1.76 -> 0.8, q0.2 2.17 -> 1.0, rip 2.23 -> 1.0). A single PSNR number was NOT sufficient and would have shipped a blur: it rises monotonically to full strength on every compressed source and never turns over. Splitting the score by how much detail the GROUND TRUTH carries at each pixel settles it — on a clean plate denoise damages BOTH halves (-15.6 dB detailed, -5.9 dB flat at full strength, the signature of a blur) while on a compressed source BOTH halves improve (q0.2 at full: +0.264 dB detailed, +0.763 dB flat), which a blur cannot do. The split is defined on the clean original so it shares no null space with the filter being tuned
